prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has passed all the previous subjects in the degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Be original in the development and application of ideas, within a research environment.
Solution of problem in new and unfamiliar multidisciplinary environments, related to its knowledge area.
Integration of knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments and sentences parting from some information that includes ethic and social liability constraints.
Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Ability of autonomous learning.

Writing, communicating and presenting scientific documents to specialists, within the scope of the contents of the Master Degree (electric power systems, hybrid and electrical vehicles and renewable energies)
Knowledge of the principal mathematic tools used in the analysis, modelling and simulation of power systems
Use of computers and digital processors in the analysis, design, simulation, monitoring, control and supervision of power systems
Asses the risks of the use of electrical energy, as well as those of industrial installations, understanding the necessity of safety elements, protections and signaling in power systems
Identify the aspects of technical design that depend most on strategic, socio-political, economic and environmental constraints
Skills related to teamwork, recognizing different roles within a group and different ways of organizing research teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical
Ability to plan and organize work
Skills for critical reasoning, making decisions and making judgments based on information that include reflecting on social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity
Concern for quality and achievement motivation
Understanding of the importance and the area of utilization of electrical power systems
Understanding the fundamental characteristics, as well as advantages and drawbacks of electrical and hybrid traction systems compared to combustion engines
Technical-economical-environmental regulations and directives in different scopes (local, regional, national, European, etc.), which are applied to power systems
Ability to identify the participant agents in the gas and electric market, and to understand its operation considering different management strategies.
Ability to assess the environmental and social implications of the operation of the electrical markets including sustainable development concerns

To develop a research work or a scientific-technical project in the field of electrical energy conversion and power systems, in the context of one of the master lines developed in the master (electrical power systems, electric and hybrid vehicles, energy efficiency and renewable energies).
To train in skills that allow him/her to act professionally as a member of an R+D+i team, both in academic and business environments.

Apply and integrate with innovative, professional and creative criteria the knowledge acquired for the elaboration of a scientific-technical work in the field of the objectives of the master's degree.
Plan the realization of an original research work, looking for the necessary materials for its realization in an autonomous way.
Defend, justify their points of view and reason critically the decisions taken as well as the results obtained in the work carried out.

Only for technical-economic management specialty: Apply the theoretical knowledge acquired, putting it into practice in the development of a work outside the educational field, linked to the exercise of the activity in a professional, public or private, appropriate environment.
Only for technical-economic management specialty: Ability to work in multidisciplinary teams.

syllabus_topics: Original analysis report project or research project in the field of technologies covered throughout the master's degree.

assessment_methods.method: Presentation of the master thesis to a specific board of professors

assessment_rules: The assessment procedure will evaluate the developed report and the presentation of the master thesis to a specific board of professors. Instructions for this procedure are included in the Master Course regulations and University Regulations. Exceptionally, non-presential evaluation methods may be included if health conditions require it, and students will be informed of any changes.
